text: machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence.
supervised learning uses labeled examples for training.
unsupervised learning discovers patterns in unlabeled data.
deep learning uses neural networks to model complex relationships.
transformers changed natural language processing by improving sequence modeling.
sentence embeddings capture semantic meaning in dense vectors.
vector search finds documents that are similar in representation space.
information retrieval focuses on finding relevant documents for a query.
ranking systems sort candidates by relevance and usefulness.
semantic search uses meaning rather than exact lexical overlap.
keyword search is effective when terms match directly.
tf idf measures term importance across a corpus.
cosine similarity compares vectors by angle rather than magnitude.
euclidean distance compares vectors by geometric distance.
gradient descent updates model parameters to reduce loss.
neural networks process information through layers of neurons.
attention mechanisms allow models to focus on important tokens.
large language models generate text by predicting the next token.
retrieval augmented generation combines search with generation.
prompt engineering improves model responses with better instructions.
fine tuning adapts a pretrained model to a specific task.
embedding models convert text into dense numerical representations.
sparse vectors store mostly zeros with explicit nonzero entries.
dense vectors store values across many dimensions.
recommender systems suggest items based on user preferences.
chatbots answer questions using language understanding and context.
search engines index documents so they can be retrieved quickly.
classification assigns inputs to known categories.
clustering groups similar examples without labels.
regression predicts numeric values from input features.
feature engineering improves model inputs before training.
evaluation metrics include precision recall and accuracy.
overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data.
underfitting happens when a model is too simple for the task.
regularization reduces model complexity to improve generalization.
cross validation estimates how a model will perform on unseen data.
natural language understanding interprets user intent from text.
named entity recognition identifies people places and organizations.
sentiment analysis detects positive or negative opinions.
question answering retrieves or generates an answer to a question.
document ranking orders evidence by relevance to a query.
semantic similarity measures conceptual closeness between texts.
language modeling predicts likely words in context.
tokenization splits text into smaller units for processing.
normalization standardizes text before analysis.
stemming reduces words to their base forms.
lemmatization maps words to dictionary forms.
indexing organizes data so retrieval is efficient.
sparse retrieval uses inverted indices for fast lookup.
dense retrieval uses embeddings for semantic matching.
hybrid retrieval combines keyword and semantic methods.
knowledge graphs represent entities and their relationships.
memory modules help systems retain important context.
dialogue systems manage multi turn conversations.
safety filters reduce harmful or manipulative outputs.
benchmarking compares systems on standard tasks.
evaluation datasets provide ground truth for testing.
confidence scores estimate how certain a prediction is.
explainability helps users understand model decisions.
model compression reduces size and inference cost.
distributed training trains models across multiple devices.
